title: Add GitHub Copilot CLI Agent in Xcode 27 via Agent Client Protocol (ACP)
description:
Apple’s Xcode 27 adds full Agent Client Protocol (ACP) support, letting developers bring third-party coding agents into Xcode beyond the built-in Claude, OpenAI, and Gemini options. The video walks through configuring the GitHub Copilot CLI as a custom ACP agent by adding its absolute path and the --acp argument in Xcode Settings - Intelligence, then starting a new conversation with Copilot inside Xcode. It demonstrates querying the model in use, generating an app overview, running a build through Xcode’s tools, and queuing a feature-planning request while the build runs, plus starting additional conversations for refactoring tasks. The creator notes limitations around skills, modes, and model switching in ACP chat, but shows changing the model via the Copilot CLI and using Copilot’s standalone Xcode integration alongside this setup.

GitHub Copilot for Xcode: https://github.com/github/CopilotForXcode

Docs: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/acp-server

title: GitHub Copilot CLI Just Went Remote — This Changes Everything
description:
GitHub just launched remote control for Copilot CLI sessions, letting you monitor and steer your terminal from the web or GitHub Mobile. When you start a session with copilot --remote, the CLI streams live output and gives you a link or QR code so you can jump in from another device. You can review plans, send follow‑up commands, switch modes, and approve permissions — all synced in real time. It’s perfect for long‑running tasks, letting you step away from your machine without losing visibility or control. This video walks through how it works and why it’s a game‑changer for developers on the go.

Remote: https://github.blog/changelog/2026-04-13-remote-control-cli-sessions-on-web-and-mobile-in-public-preview/

description:
The VS Code team has introduced a new integrated browser that upgrades the old Simple Browser by letting you open and interact with webpages directly inside VS Code, with full DevTools, logs you can add to chat in one click, element selection for AI prompt context, and screenshot support. The script demos running Scott Hanselman’s Tiny Tool Town (an Astro site), inspecting the DOM and DevTools, and comparing Simple Browser’s limitations to the new browser, which can also handle server apps and sites like github.com for scenarios such as authentication testing. It also shows enabling chat tools so a chat agent can be shared the browser, navigate and test flows (optionally using Playwright), and implement a new count-up widget across pages while repeatedly validating changes in real time.

00:00 Productivity Boost Intro
00:18 What the Integrated Browser Does
01:16 Demo Setup Tiny Tool Town
02:20 Simple Browser Basics
03:00 Limitations and Why Upgrade
03:12 New Integrated Browser Tour
04:04 Make It the Default Browser
04:28 Enable Agent Browser Tools
04:57 Agent Driven Navigation Demo
05:56 Build and Verify Count Up Widget
07:45 Wrap Up and Next Steps

title: The GitHub Copilot SDK IS INSANE! Put Copilot INSIDE Your Apps!
description:
Announcement blog: https://github.blog/news-insights/company-news/build-an-agent-into-any-app-with-the-github-copilot-sdk/?utm_source=blog-announcement-cli-sdk&utm_medium=&utm_campaign=cli-sdk-jan-2026

GitHub Copilot isn’t just in your editor anymore—this episode dives into the new Copilot SDK (now in technical preview) and how it lets you embed the Copilot CLI’s agent power directly into your own apps. You’ll see what’s possible with session management, model switching, streaming, and tool calling, plus a real demo: a .NET “podcast metadata generator” that cranks out titles, descriptions, and YouTube chapters from a transcript in minutes.

Links: 
Copilot CLI: https://github.com/github/copilot-cli
Copilot SDK: https://github.com/github/copilot-sdk
Samples: https://github.com/jamesmontemagno/hello-copilot-sdk-dotnet & https://github.com/jamesmontemagno/podcast-metadata-generator
